title: Returned Goods Condition and Clawback Merchandise Value (Contract Pricing Agreement Rebates)
content:
Returned goods condition and the merchandise value used for a Contract Pricing Agreement rebate clawback

When volume rebate on a Contract Pricing Agreement is clawed back for a return, the clawback's merchandise value — the figure the rebate rate is applied to — follows the condition the return receipt recorded for the goods. The receipt is the one recorded for that return on the customer's Ship-To Fulfillment Account records, which show the item condition found, the quantity received, the invoiced unit price, any restocking fee deducted and the return credit determined.

| Condition recorded on the receipt | Clawback's merchandise value |
|---|---|
| Goods opened but unused | The quantity received multiplied by the invoiced unit price |
| Goods unopened and resaleable, with a restocking fee deducted | The return credit plus that restocking fee |
| Every other return (including unopened and resaleable goods with no restocking fee deducted) | The return credit |

**Cases (hypothetical figures).**
- 10 units received opened but unused, invoiced at 25.00 each, return credit 200.00: merchandise value 10 multiplied by 25.00, which is 250.00.
- Goods unopened and resaleable, return credit 225.00 after a restocking fee of 25.00: merchandise value 225.00 plus 25.00, which is 250.00.
- Goods found defective, return credit 180.00: merchandise value 180.00.
